titulo: Gustar and preferences: Free time and conversation

aula.objetivo: Talk about what you like and don't like with gustar and encantar, agree and disagree with «a mí también / tampoco / sí / no», give a simple opinion, ask «¿qué te gusta?», and talk about free time.

blocos.titulo: Asking about likes, playing and performing
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: to ask a friend: «¿Qué te gusta hacer?» (what do you like to do?), «¿Te gusta el cine?», «¿Qué música te gusta?». With «usted»: «¿Qué le gusta hacer?». STEP 2: to choose between two or more things, use «¿Cuál?» («which one») and «¿Cuáles?» («which ones»): «¿Cuál prefieres?», «¿Cuáles te gustan?». Before a noun, use «qué»: «¿Qué color prefieres?» (what color do you prefer?). STEP 3: «jugar a» + a game or sport: «Juego al fútbol» (I play soccer), «Jugamos a las cartas» (we play cards). «Tocar» + an instrument: «Toco la guitarra» (I play guitar), «Toca el piano» (he/she plays piano). You can't say «jugar la guitarra». STEP 4: «leer, ver series, salir con amigos, viajar, cocinar, ir al gimnasio, pasear» are free-time activities (to read, watch shows, go out with friends, travel, cook, go to the gym, go for a walk). STEP 5: false friends: «exquisito» means delicious, and a cake can be «exquisita»; to say something's odd or weird, use «raro» or «extraño». Watch out too for «divertido»: it covers both «fun» and «funny». STEP 6: a full answer keeps the dialogue going: «Me gusta mucho porque es relajante» (I like it a lot because it's relaxing). Add the reason with «porque».
blocos.comparacao: English «exquisite» and Spanish «exquisito» look like a direct match, but they aren't: English «exquisite» means finely made or refined, while Spanish «exquisito» simply means delicious — food, not craftsmanship. The word that actually means «odd, strange» in Spanish is «raro», which has no visual resemblance to any false-friend trap in English at all.

tabela.sentido: [misto] to play a sport or game

erros.motivo: Sports and games are «played» with «jugar», plus «a».

blocos.titulo: Mi tiempo libre / My free time
blocos.ru: Me llamo Daniel y tengo veintiocho años. Entre semana trabajo mucho y casi no tengo tiempo libre, pero los fines de semana me gusta salir con mis amigos. Me encanta jugar al fútbol, y a mi amiga Clara le gusta tocar la guitarra. A mí no me gustan las series largas; prefiero ver una película y cocinar después. Los domingos nos gusta comer en un restaurante pequeño donde la comida es exquisita. A Clara le parece un lugar raro, pero a mí me parece muy divertido.
blocos.pt: My name is Daniel and I'm twenty-eight years old. During the week I work a lot and barely have any free time, but on weekends I like going out with my friends. I love playing soccer, and my friend Clara likes playing guitar. I don't like long series; I'd rather watch a movie and cook afterward. On Sundays we like eating at a little restaurant where the food is delicious. For Clara it's a weird place, but for me it's a lot of fun.

blocos.enunciado: Write and say out loud five sentences about your free time: what you like, what you prefer, what your friends like, and what you find boring. Use a «porque» at least once.
Ask a friend three questions with «¿Te gusta…?» or «¿Te gustan…?» and answer them yourself.
